title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: X/S is a smooth relative curve. P_X is the étale sheaf of étale S-maps U→P^1_S (local 'projective coordinates'). H = PGL_2 = Aut(P^1_S) acts on P_X. The previous page built the torsor Conn_{X/S} of relative projective connections (P^1-structures) under ω^{⊗2}_{X/S}. It also built a canonical map c^X: P_X → Conn_{X/S}, c^X(t) = t^*(c), where c is the unique projective connection on P^1_S. The difference G(t,s) = c^X(s) − c^X(t) ∈ ω^{⊗2} is an abstract Schwarzian derivative.

(1) Characteristic 0. Take étale maps s,t: X → X_0, with X_0 a P^1-bundle over S. If G(t,s)=0, i.e. t^*c_{X_0} = s^*c_{X_0}, then s = g∘t for some g ∈ Aut(X_0). This is the classical fact that vanishing Schwarzian means Möbius. Two consequences follow. For fixed t, the map f^*(H_S)\P_X → ω^{⊗2}, s ↦ G(t,s), is injective. Intrinsically, the induced map C^X: H\P_X → Conn_{X/S} is injective but not surjective. A projective connection in its image is called 'intégrable par fonctions algébriques': étale-locally it is induced by an algebraic étale coordinate.

(2) Characteristic p. Introduce the relative Frobenius F_X: X → X^{(p/S)}. Möbius transformations with coefficients in (the germ of) O_{X^{(p)}} leave G(t,s) invariant. So injectivity can at best hold for F_X^{-1}(H_{X^{(p)}})\P_X → Conn_{X/S}; this is proved on the next page for p ≠ 2,3. This is exactly the notion later called Frobenius-projective structures / dormant PGL_2-opers.

(3) Integral form. Use Hasse–Schmidt derivatives D^{(n)}_t f = (1/n!) d^n f/dt^n with respect to an étale coordinate t; these make sense in any characteristic. The page gives G(t,s) = 12·G_0(t,s), with G_0 = −D^{(3)}s/D^{(1)}s + (D^{(2)}s/D^{(1)}s)^2. Hence Conn_{X/S} is the pushout, along 12·id: ω^{⊗2} → ω^{⊗2}, of a finer torsor Conn_{0,X/S}. This finer torsor carries a map c_0^X: P_{X/S} → Conn_0 with c_0^X(s) − c_0^X(t) = G_0(t,s). It is an integral Schwarzian torsor that stays meaningful when 12 = 0 on S. When 12·1_S = 0, all c^X(t) coincide, giving a 'canonical' projective connection in the naive sense.

Purpose: to set up a characteristic-free theory of projective structures on relative curves inside the Gauss–Manin / Picard–Fuchs / Cartier dossier. Presumably the aim is to compare algebraic integrability in characteristic 0 with Frobenius-type integrability mod p.
errors: Normalization: with S(s) = s'''/s' − (3/2)(s''/s')^2, one gets G_0 = −S/6, so G = 12 G_0 = −2S. This is consistent with the previous-page normalization only up to sign and convention; the page does not check it explicitly.

The 'canonical projective connection' when 12·1_S = 0 is merely the trivialisation of a torsor pushed out along the zero map. It is not an intrinsic structure; Grothendieck implicitly recognises this by passing to Conn_0.

In char p the claimed invariance of G under PGL_2(O_{X^{(p)}}) is fine (for p = 2,3 trivially, since G = 0). However, G_0 is NOT invariant under Möbius maps with p-th-power coefficients when p = 2,3. For example, in char 2, D^{(2)}(α^2) = (D^{(1)}α)^2 ≠ 0. For p = 2,3 one needs p^2-th powers. The next-page margin reading 'O^{(p^3)}' is probably p^2 (or a transcription error).
The global statement s = g∘t needs X connected (relative to S) and possibly étale localisation on S to get g over S; this is unstated.

ideas.what: Projective connections on a relative curve as a torsor under ω^{⊗2}, with a canonical map from local étale coordinates; the difference is the Schwarzian
ideas.modern_name: projective structures / PGL_2-opers; Schwarzian derivative as torsor difference
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (Schwarz, Poincaré); algebraic form Gunning (1960s), Beilinson–Drinfeld opers (1990s)

ideas.what: Vanishing Schwarzian ⇒ Möbius; injectivity of H\P_X → Conn; image = projective connections 'integrable by algebraic functions'
ideas.modern_name: projective structures with algebraic developing map / finite projective monodromy (Schwarz list, Lamé equations)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; Baldassarri–Dwork (1979) for algebraic solutions of 2nd-order ODEs

ideas.what: In char p, quotient by Möbius group over O_{X^{(p)}} via relative Frobenius; expected injectivity
ideas.modern_name: Frobenius-projective structures / dormant indigenous bundles (p-curvature zero)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Ihara (Schwarzian equations, 1974), Mochizuki (p-adic Teichmüller theory, 1990s), Hoshi (Frobenius-projective structures, 2010s)

ideas.what: Integral Schwarzian via Hasse–Schmidt derivatives, G = 12·G_0, and a finer torsor Conn_0 of which the naive one is the 12-pushout, valid in characteristics 2 and 3
ideas.modern_name: integral/Hasse–Schmidt Schwarzian; projective structures in char 2, 3
ideas.usually_credited_to: unsure (char 2/3 projective structures studied by Hoshi, Wakabayashi in 2010s)

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, in the 1970s and before Mochizuki, a characteristic-free theory of projective structures on relative curves. It includes a char-p Frobenius-twisted rigidity statement (Schwarzian zero ⇒ Möbius over O^p), i.e. Frobenius-projective / dormant structures, placed in a dossier on Gauss–Manin, Picard–Fuchs and the Cartier operator.
missed.quote: le mieux qu'on puisse espérer, c'est d'avoir F_X^{-1}(H_{X^{(p/S)}})^{|P}X ⟶ Conn_{X/S} [injectif]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early, independent formulation of Frobenius-projective structures and dormant opers. It is relevant to the history of p-adic Teichmüller theory and to crediting Ihara/Grothendieck-era ideas.

missed.claim: The juxtaposition of 'intégrable par fonctions algébriques' (char 0) with Frobenius-integrability mod p implicitly suggests a Grothendieck–Katz-type criterion for projective connections. The suggested statement: a projective structure is algebraically integrable iff its reductions are Frobenius-projective (dormant) for almost all p.
missed.quote: Une conn. affine qui est dans l'image de _H^{|P}X est dite "intégrable par fonctions algébriques". Si S est de car. p>0 ...
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is the p-curvature conjecture specialised to opers / Schwarzian equations. It is known in some cases (e.g. Katz for Picard–Fuchs), but this oper-theoretic phrasing is rarely tied to Grothendieck.

missed.claim: A refinement of the torsor of projective connections to an integral torsor Conn_0 (Hasse–Schmidt Schwarzian G_0 = G/12) that remains meaningful in characteristics 2 and 3.
missed.quote: le torseur Conn_{X/S} est déduit ... ω^{⊗2} --12 id--> ω^{⊗2}, d'un torseur plus fin Conn_{0 X/S}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Char 2/3 projective structures and opers are a current topic (Hoshi, Wakabayashi). An explicit integral torsor with this normalization may not be recorded with this attribution.

deep.surprise_reason: Not a new theorem: the content is classical or rediscovered. But Grothendieck's c.1972–81 algebraic, torsor-theoretic treatment of projective structures, the char-p Frobenius-twisted rigidity, and the integral Schwarzian refinement for p = 2,3 anticipate Mochizuki/Hoshi-style theory and seem absent from his published record.
transcription_corrections: 'X est épaisseur globale' likely reads something like 'X est (une) épaisseur globale' or an unreadable phrase; the reference '(cf. lettre 15.3)' is uncertain.
'défini au droite projective' should be read 'fibré en droites projectives sur S' (X_0 a P^1-bundle).
Margin 'univoque!' is probably 'à vérifier!' or a similar check mark.
'moyennant le dégât de Cung' is likely 'moyennant le changement de groupe d'opérateurs' (pushout along 12·id).
Next page margin 'O^{(p^3)}' should mathematically be O^{(p^2)} for p = 2,3.
